spec.title: Lag per partition
spec.description: ep_consumer_lag by partition. With the DLQ off, the poison partition (5) should climb and never come down while the other five stay near 0. With the DLQ on it should show a short bump and return to 0. Surprising: other partitions also growing (the consumer is too slow for the rate, then the run is not about the poison).

spec.title: Committed offset per partition
spec.description: ep_consumer_last_committed_offset by partition. A flat line on one partition while the others rise means that partition is blocked. Surprising: all lines flat (consumer not running) or the poison partition flat with the DLQ on.

spec.title: Run phase
spec.description: ep_k6_phase (ADDED BY K6, written by run.sh to the node_exporter textfile): 0 load running, 1 poison written, 2 observation after the load, -1 between runs. Shows where the poison went in.

spec.title: Events in vs rows written
spec.description: k6 202 rate (events that must be stored) against rows inserted by the consumer. With the DLQ off the inserted line falls below the input by about one sixth after the poison. With the DLQ on they match.

spec.title: Messages consumed per second
spec.description: rate of ep_consumer_messages_consumed_total (counts records of completed chunks). With the DLQ off the poison partition adds nothing. Surprising: a very high rate with few rows inserted (the same records being counted again and again).

spec.title: Failed chunk attempts by reason
spec.description: rate of ep_consumer_chunk_failures_total by reason. With the DLQ off, poison_blocked should be a steady hot loop (tens per second, not one per backoff step). With the DLQ on it should stay about 0.

spec.title: Retries by class and bad records by class
spec.description: ep_consumer_retries_total and ep_consumer_errors_total by class. With the DLQ on: PERMANENT_PARSE should have 0 retries (the parser error is final), PERMANENT_DB / UNKNOWN should show about SINK_MAX_RETRIES (3) retries per poison record.

spec.title: Records published to the DLQ
spec.description: ep_consumer_dlq_total by error_class. Should step to 1 per run in the DLQ-on cells and stay 0 when it is off. Surprising: more than 1 (the poison being dead-lettered twice, or good rows dead-lettered).

spec.title: Chunk processing time p99
spec.description: Whole chunk: parse + write + DLQ + offset commit. The retries with backoff of a PERMANENT_DB poison show up here as a longer chunk (about 100 + 200 + 400 ms plus jitter at most). Surprising: seconds.

spec.title: Freshness p99
spec.description: Age of a row when it becomes visible (DB commit time minus received_at). A blocked partition produces no new rows, so the line shows the other partitions only. After a drain (DLQ on) a short rise is expected.

spec.title: Consumer process CPU
spec.description: user and system CPU seconds per second of the consumer process. A hot retry loop (DLQ off) should use more CPU than the DLQ-on run at the same input. The consumer is pinned to 2 CPUs, so 2.0 is the ceiling.

spec.title: Host CPU busy of the pinned groups
spec.description: 100 x (1 - idle) over the CPUs of each group (variables cpu_server, cpu_consumer, cpu_k6). Keep k6 under about 70%.

spec.title: Postgres connection wait
spec.description: ep_pg_pool_waiting of the consumer. Should stay about 0; a stuck partition should not touch the database.

spec.title: k6 dropped iterations
spec.description: Must be 0. Any value means the generator, not the system, fell behind; discard the run.

spec.title: k6 failed requests and request p99
spec.description: k6_http_req_failed_rate should be 0 (the API does not know about the poison). Note: k6 series are not marked stale after a run, the last value can linger.

spec.title: Event loop lag p99
spec.description: nodejs_eventloop_lag_p99_seconds of the API and the consumer. A busy-looping consumer would show here first. Surprising: above about 0.1 s.

spec.title: API acknowledged messages
spec.description: rate of ep_kafka_messages_acked_total, must equal the k6 202 rate. The API must not notice the poison.

spec.title: 1. The verdict: does the poison partition stop, and do the others go on?
2. The mechanism: retry loop, retries and the dead letter
3. Resource view: what the stuck loop costs

spec.name: cpu_server
spec.label: CPUs: server (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the server group is pinned to (0,6), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_server"

spec.name: cpu_consumer
spec.label: CPUs: consumer (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the consumer group is pinned to (1,7), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_consumer"

spec.name: cpu_k6
spec.label: CPUs: k6 (pinned)
spec.description: CPU ids the k6 group is pinned to (4,10), as a regex for cpu=~"$cpu_k6"
